clue.text: Managed currencies? Right shambles

indicators.note: letters that are managed are handled and arranged anew, so the words that follow are reordered

explanation.surface: An economist declares a system of controlled exchange rates a complete mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed currencies' reads as an economics term, but 'Managed' only signals the rearrangement of both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-ring circus is an idiom for a chaotic, noisy scene, just like a shambles.

clue.text: One finding an actor a job in camp, a man

definitions.text: One finding an actor a job

parts.note: camp behaviour is exaggerated and theatrical
an agent is a man who acts on someone else's behalf

explanation.surface: Someone lands a performer work at a holiday camp, and that someone is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical agent is the representative who secures roles and bookings for performers.

clue.text: Message received from a boy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the radio operator's word confirming a transmission got through

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges a message sent by a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure the reply word signals understanding, and it is also a common male first name.

clue.text: Simple first principle a railway follows

indicators.note: follows says the later pieces come after the earlier one in the answer

parts.note: an element is a basic principle of a subject
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A railway plan is built on a simple founding rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary describes something basic and easy, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: One politician is on about Republican being put away

explanation.surface: A politician keeps banging on about a Republican who has been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is loose here: 'is on about Republican' is meant to put the Republican's R first, with the two little words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is an idiom for locking them up in jail.

clue.text: Country shown in film, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, so we want a word sounding like the film's title

explanation.surface: A country is featured in a movie, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Clue may be perfect, though short

indicators.note: short says the word for perfect is cut and loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A crossword clue can be flawless even when it is brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint, and having an idea of something means having a hint about it.

clue.text: London street in inexpensive quarter

parts.note: a side of town is a quarter or district

explanation.surface: A London road found in the cheaper part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAPSIDE is a historic street in the City of London, once a market.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapside is a well-known thoroughfare in the City of London.

clue.text: Bridge partners fencing inside college? Possibly it's best to say nothing

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so the partners go round the following words
possibly hints that the letters could be set out another way

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Two card players fence at university, and maybe discretion is wisest.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that keeping quiet is often more valuable than speaking.

clue.text: Bird nesting in one, a glen

indicators.note: nesting in says the bird sits tucked inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A bird makes its nest in a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey that nests in highland glens.

clue.text: Part flour, a little at a time

explanation.surface: A recipe of some flour added in small amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal describes doing something gradually, in stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Sort of suite, extremely expensive? The price is staggering!

indicators.note: something staggering lurches about unsteadily, so these letters are thrown out of order
extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shopper is shocked at the cost of a furniture suite.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-piece suite is a sofa with two matching armchairs.

clue.text: Run out from square leg

explanation.surface: A cricket dismissal effected by a fielder at square leg, a position level with the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket; 'Run out' is really a short drive or trip, a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a brief outing in a car, a quick run out.

clue.text: Fundamental teaching hospital in her street, demolished

indicators.note: in says the hospital sits inside the words that come next
a demolished building is broken up, so these letters are knocked down and rebuilt

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A teaching hospital on her road has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The three Rs are the basic skills of schooling, so they are the fundamentals of education.

clue.text: Moving home, a Poet Laureate

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Andrew Motion was Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: A Poet Laureate is moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in motion is under way, travelling, which is what moving means.

clue.text: The Italian with a musical intrument seen in Maine, or Wisconsin city

indicators.note: seen in places the earlier pieces within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: postal abbreviation of the US state

explanation.surface: An Italian with an instrument turns up in Maine, or perhaps in a Wisconsin city.
explanation.definitionFit: Milwaukee is the largest city in the US state of Wisconsin.

clue.text: Appear clearly round rear of minster, a place of worship

indicators.note: round says one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: to shine is to stand out clearly

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A minster's back stands out brightly as a place for prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy site where people come to venerate or worship.

clue.text: Left-hander shot up excitedly, getting a wicket

indicators.note: acting excitedly means jumping about wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A left-handed bowler leaps in delight after taking a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is slang for a left-handed person, especially a boxer or pitcher.

clue.text: Appeal of seduction after a bit of lust

indicators.note: after says the first-named piece comes later in the answer
a bit of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: a lure is a temptation or enticement

explanation.surface: Seduction gains its appeal from a touch of desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness or charm, the appeal something holds.

clue.text: Appropriate to lock blockhouse

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Something suitable for securing a fortified building.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhouse is a small military stronghold, a kind of fort.

clue.text: Guess amount

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reckon or work out
second meaning: a sum or number

explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to reckon or suppose, and a figure is a numerical total or sum.

clue.text: A street apart

parts.note: way is a word for a road or street

explanation.definitionFit: Away means at a distance, separate from something, just as apart does.

clue.text: French writer, first to embrace Oscar

parts.note: the victor comes first in a contest
O is Oscar in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A French author was the first to hug an Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables.

clue.text: Part of ground amazingly free from obstruction

indicators.note: part of says the letters are taken from inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Some land has amazingly been cleared of obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: To undam a river is to remove the barrier, freeing it from obstruction.

clue.text: Such an irritation for Cockney to get married

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: getting hitched is slang for marrying

explanation.surface: A Londoner finds the idea of marriage terribly annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class speech of East London, known for dropping the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a tickling skin sensation, a mild irritation.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise from Miss Sharp failing to open box

indicators.note: failing to open means the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Becky Sharp is the heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair
to box is to punch, to thump

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when Miss Sharp cannot get a box open.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an old northern English (Lancashire) exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecky thump is a dialect interjection expressing astonishment.

clue.text: Stopped over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: came to a halt

explanation.definitionFit: Ended is the past tense of end, meaning stopped, and as a participle it means finished.

clue.text: Bearers of gifts, seen with her, meet abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so these letters are spread out and regathered

explanation.surface: People bringing presents are seen with her, meeting overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the Nativity story brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.
